entries.name: Cook's Assistant
entries.summary: The head cook of Lumbridge Castle forgot to buy the ingredients for Duke Horacio's birthday cake and roped in the first adventurer through the kitchen door. That was you. He kept his job, and you got the use of his range.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
You walked into the castle kitchen and found the head cook in a panic. It was the Duke's birthday, the cook was meant to be baking the cake, and he had forgotten to buy the ingredients. He was certain the Duke would sack him, and he had four children and a goat to feed. His words.

The list was a bucket of milk, an egg and a pot of flour. He sent you to Millie Miller for the flour, Gillie Groats for the milk, and the Groats' farm or any chicken for the egg. Any chicken. He was past being particular.

The egg first, from the chicken coop. Nothing to it. Then the milk: you took an empty bucket into the cow field and used it on the dairy cow. Gillie Groats will explain milking if asked; it's a cow and a bucket, but the offer stands.

Then the flour, which took the most steps. You picked grain in the wheat field, tipped it into the hopper at Mill Lane Mill, pulled the lever, and filled an empty pot from the flour bin. Millie Miller explains how it works, should the lever not explain itself.

You brought all three back and the cook declared himself saved. You asked whether you could come to the Duke's party. He said only important people dine with nobility, and that perhaps one day you would be one of them, though he doubted it. I have underlined 'doubted'.

Then he let you use his range. He calls it the Cook-o-matic 100, and it burns fewer foods than an ordinary range. Somebody in that kitchen needed to.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
The cook, described, with no great effort, as "The head cook of Lumbridge castle."

{done:A_TAIL_OF_TWO_CATS} As for his family: he claims a wife, four children and a goat. Bob the cat says he has no children at all.

Duke Horacio, the Duke of Lumbridge, whose birthday it was. Never seen during the quest; he lives on the first floor of the castle, one floor up from the trouble.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Lumbridge Castle kitchen, ground floor. The cook, his range, and a pot that is always on the centre table.

Lumbridge Castle cellar, down the kitchen trapdoor. There is always a bucket.

The chicken coop, for the egg: east out of the castle, north up the path, north-west of Farmer Fred's house. That house was the whole of Fred's part.

The Lumbridge cow field, across the River Lum. The dairy cow with the cowbell, and Gillie Groats beside it.

The wheat field south-west of the cow field. The grain.

Mill Lane Mill. Hopper and lever on the top floor, flour bin on the ground floor, Millie Miller inside.

Lumbridge General Store. Buckets and pots, if you arrive with neither.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The errand sends you all round Lumbridge. It's a shopping list doing the work of a map, and doing it well.

It wasn't his first cake, either. He has tried, and failed, more times than anyone has bothered to count.

{done:DEATH_TO_THE_DORGESHUUN} In Death to the Dorgeshuun, when you introduce Zanik to him, he tries to offer her the very same errand. You tell him she has no time and he says it was worth a try.

{done:DEATH_TO_THE_DORGESHUUN} The histories take this to mean he asks every newcomer, and so do I. The cook at the Servants' Guild in Ardougne complains that she was fired overnight and replaced by a fool who cannot bake a cake without help. The description fits.

{done:RECIPE_FOR_DISASTER__ANOTHER_COOKS_QUEST} The kitchen has history. The cook's ancestor Franizzard Van Lumbcook won the post of head cook for life a century ago by impressing the Lumbridge council with a banquet.

{done:RECIPE_FOR_DISASTER} Recipe for Disaster follows on from this one. The cook tries to recreate that banquet for the council's ten-yearly meeting, and the Culinaromancer crashes the feast. He's a cook with a grudge, shut in another dimension a hundred years before.

Lumbridge itself was settled by human nomads who bridged the River Lum, which is where the name comes from. The rest, from the first Duke onward, is on the Lumbridge page. Nobody in the kitchen brought it up.

As for the range, adventurers call it the Lumbridge Castle range. The foods it burns less often run from bread and shrimps up to salmon, and it is especially good for mushroom and botanical pies.

{done:A_TAIL_OF_TWO_CATS} Bob the cat praises the cook's old fashioned seafood gumbo, an old family recipe. So the man can cook. He cannot bake, which is a different complaint.

One last note. You can buy all three ingredients on the Grand Exchange before talking to the cook and finish the quest in seconds. Which rather defeats the map.

people: Gillie Groats - the milkmaid, optional
Millie Miller - the miller, optional; of the two explanations, hers is worth hearing
details: Rewards - 1 quest point, 300 Cooking experience and the use of the Cook-o-matic 100

plates.caption: Lumbridge, where it began.
plates.hint: Pose for me in Lumbridge.

entries.name: Priest in Peril
entries.summary: King Roald sent you to check on Drezel, the priest at Paterdomus, because the temple had gone quiet. Monks of Zamorak had taken it, and they talked you into killing the Temple Guardian so they could poison the Salve.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
Paterdomus is the temple to Saradomin on Misthalin's eastern border. King Roald told you the blessed waters of the River Salve beneath it are what keep the vampyres of Morytania out.

Nobody had heard from Drezel, and Roald asked you to go and check on him. I wrote down 'check'. It turned out to be a small word for the job.

At the temple door a voice asked who you were and what you wanted. When you said the King had sent you, a second voice introduced itself as Drevil, then hurriedly corrected that to Drezel. 'Drevil' went into the notes with a question mark, and nobody consulted them.

This so-called Drezel said a horrible big dog-like thing had moved into the mausoleum outside and asked you to get rid of it. You killed the Temple Guardian down there, "a big ugly dog" by common account. The description was unkind; so, in the end, were we. The dog has its own page.

Back at the palace, King Roald was furious. The dog was no pest: it guarded the mausoleum entrance and the source of the Salve, and with it dead anyone could sabotage the river's blessing.

He called it treason and threatened to have you beheaded, then relented and ordered you to put it right. I took those minutes very quietly.

Back at the temple you climbed to the top floor and found the real Drezel, locked in a cell. Through the bars he told you Zamorakians had attacked the temple to desecrate the blessing the Seven Priestly Warriors had placed on the Salve, and had brought a trapped vampyre up into a coffin near his cell. The key to his cell, he thought, was with the hooded one.

Back downstairs you fought the hooded monk and took the golden key he dropped. It did not fit Drezel's door; the real one was hidden somewhere. The monks have their own page.

In the mausoleum again, the golden key opened the room of seven monuments round the well. Searching them turned up the iron key, which you swapped for the golden one. You filled a bucket with murky water from the well, and murky was the polite word.

The iron key opened Drezel's cell. He blessed the water and you poured it over the coffin outside his cell, sealing the vampyre inside. It did not thank you.

Below, Drezel explained that the Zamorakians had used a potion to pollute the Salve. While he reinforced the barrier, you were to soak up the evil magic it had released, with essence. Hand him the essence outright and he skips the speech. It goes down as giving the priest your blank runes, and I haven't corrected it.

When it was done he gave you Wolfbane, a silver dagger passed down through his family for generations and imbued with the power of Saradomin. The dagger gets its own paragraph further down. It earned it.

He warned of the vampyres and werewolves beyond and mentioned the Myreque resistance. To cross, you ask him for permission to pass and wait for his blessing; he is a priest, and there is a form.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
King Roald: Roald Remanis III, ruler of Misthalin, at home in Varrock Palace. The dog was his, and he called it Spots. The histories call him a steady, straightforward king, and Varrock has done well under him.

Drezel: described, and briefly, as "A holy man." A priest of Saradomin, descended from one of the Seven Priestly Warriors. Use a spare iron key on his old cell door and he asks what you are trying to lock him back in for, which is a fair question.

{done:IN_AID_OF_THE_MYREQUE,DARKNESS_OF_HALLOWVALE,SINS_OF_THE_FATHER} Drezel later works with the Myreque in In Aid of the Myreque, Darkness of Hallowvale and Sins of the Father.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Varrock Palace: King Roald's audience room, in the south-east corner by the main entrance. There is always a bucket in the palace bedroom.

Silvarea: the mountain pass in north-east Misthalin, past the Earth altar, ending at the temple.

Paterdomus: the temple on the River Salve, held by the monks from the ground floor up, with Drezel's cell on the top floor.

The mausoleum: down the trapdoor north of the temple. The guardian's chamber, the seven-monument room with the well behind the southern gate, and the north-east passage where Drezel settles.

The River Salve: the blessed river that forms Misthalin's border with Morytania. The temple bridge is the only crossing.

Morytania and Canifis: the werewolf town just east of the temple, and the land beyond it, both opened by the quest.

Varrock Museum: Historian Minas and the Kudos.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The Seven Priestly Warriors have their own page, where I wrote their names out in full, and Morytania has its own, history and all.

{done:THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES} The blessing on the Salve was not what the soldiers were told.

Wolfbane: "A silver dagger that can prevent werewolves changing form." The citizens of Canifis turn into werewolves when attacked, unless you wield it. It cannot be poisoned, you can only hold one, and Drezel replaces it.

{done:NATURE_SPIRIT} Drezel next sends you into Mort Myre Swamp with meat and apple pies for the druid Filliman Tarlock, in Nature Spirit.

people: Monk of Zamorak - level 30, the hooded impostor at the door
Temple Guardian - level 30, the dog in the mausoleum
Historian Minas - did not ask to see my notes. Nobody does.

Kudos - 5, from Historian Minas

Essence - 50 rune or pure, in one trip with pouches or several without

Wolfbane - a silver weapon, so it works on tier 1 vampyres

entries.name: Waterfall Quest
entries.summary: Almera asked you to fetch her son Hudon back from treasure hunting on the river at Baxtorian Falls. You never did get him home, but you found the treasure he was after, so I have filed the errand as a success, loosely.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
Almera was worried about her son Hudon. He cannot swim, and had already fallen in three times. You took her log raft, which wrecked on a small island, and there he was. He refused to come home, said he would find the treasure soon, and turned down your help on the grounds that you would only steal it.

You swam south and washed ashore by the Tourist Information Centre. Gerald and Hadley tell the story between them: an ancient elven king who shut himself in his secret home under the waterfall after his wife was captured and killed by invaders.

Upstairs was the Book on Baxtorian, which you had to read, and I read over your shoulder. It says Baxtorian and Glarial were elves, that a treasure lies under the falls, and that Glarial's pebble, the key to her tomb, was taken by a gnome family over a century ago. Their descendants might still keep it in their cave beneath the Tree Gnome Village.

Down in that cave the gnome Golrie had locked himself in to keep the hobgoblins off his family's heirlooms, and had left the key outside. You found it in a crate and let him out. He handed over Glarial's pebble as a bit of old elven junk, keeping the key so he could lock up again.

Glarial's tombstone calls her the wife of Baxtorian and a true friend of nature, and says only visitors with peaceful intent may enter. It means it: the pebble only opens the tomb if you carry no weapons, armour, runes or ammunition.

Inside, three Moss Guardians roam alongside zombies and skeletons, and you slipped past them unarmed, which was the sensible way to do it. You took Glarial's amulet and her urn, holding her ashes, and the tomb will not let you leave without both.

Then back to Almera's, the raft again, and the wreck again. Wearing the amulet is what stops the door on the waterfall ledge washing you out.

The final chamber holds six pillars, two statues and the Chalice of Eternity, floating in the air. You used one air, one water and one earth rune on each of the six pillars, Glarial's amulet on the statue of Glarial, and the urn on the chalice, tipping her ashes in. The ground rose. I put the quill down for that part.

Baxtorian's treasure was yours. Try to take it without the ritual and you are washed out of the cavern, and you lose the amulet and the urn. As for Hudon, the errand itself: he still has not found anything, accuses you of stealing his treasure, and insists you owe him a share, because he showed you where the treasure was.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
Almera: described, and fairly, as "Nice hair." Speedy Keith gets the very same words. I checked twice.

Hudon: "Looks young." I haven't warmed to him.

Gerald: "Looks suspiciously like a fisherman," and he is one. He fishes trout and salmon by the River Dougne. He knows the story of Baxtorian's treasure, left about 200 years back at the end of the Fourth Age, and of all the adventurers who've looked for the tomb and failed. He was glad of someone to tell it to.

Hadley: described, not by me, as "Could do with losing a bit of weight." The tourist guide at the Tourist Information Centre.

{done:DESERT_TREASURE_I} He turns up again in Desert Treasure I, helping to find the Shadow Dungeon.

Golrie: "He seems to be in a spot of bother," which undersells being locked in. A gnome of the Tree Gnome Village, and the current keeper of his family's heirlooms, Glarial's pebble among them until you came along.

{done:TREE_GNOME_VILLAGE,THE_PATH_OF_GLOUPHRIE} Golrie's grandfather was King Bolrie, and his great-uncle is King Bolren, who rules the Tree Gnome Village and holds off General Khazard's army in the quest of that name.

Baxtorian: King Baxtorian, the elven king under the falls, and Glarial's husband. You do not meet him.

{done:SONG_OF_THE_ELVES} In Song of the Elves he turns out to be alive, turned to stone in the hope of one day reuniting with Glarial; he is freed and, reluctantly, becomes elder of the Cadarn clan. He is Lord Baxtorian Cadarn now. He and Glarial had a daughter, Eirlys.

Glarial: Queen Glarial, wife of Baxtorian. The elves later buried her ashes in the tomb under the protection of the Moss Guardians.

{done:ROVING_ELVES} Taking her urn left her spirit restless until Roving Elves, and that one is on us.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Almera's house: north-east of Baxtorian Falls, south of the Barbarian Outpost, with the river behind it and the raft beside it.

Baxtorian Falls: the rapids themselves, which have their own page, barrel and all. The small island is where the raft wrecks. Both times.

Tourist Information Centre: just south of the falls by Lake Baxtorian. Hadley inside, Gerald fishing outside, the Book on Baxtorian upstairs in the southernmost bookcase on the east wall.

Tree Gnome Village: south-west of Ardougne and north of Yanille, hidden inside a hedge maze.

Tree Gnome Village Dungeon: down the ladder in the maze. The east room has zombies, giant bats and the key, in the differently coloured crate in the south-east corner; the west room has Golrie and the hobgoblins.

Glarial's Tomb: south-east of the falls, north-west of the Fishing Guild, under a tombstone. The amulet is in the west chamber's chest, the urn in the south chamber's coffin.

Waterfall Dungeon: the connected caverns under the falls, reached by rope from the big grey rock downstream to a dead tree and the doors on the ledge. The eastern passage has spiders, skeletons and the key in the northernmost crate; the western has fire giants and the locked door through to the chalice room, the northernmost cavern.

Barbarian Outpost and Fishing Guild: the landmarks either side of the falls. Good for bearings.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:SONG_OF_THE_ELVES} The door is sealed because of the Elven Civil War. Baxtorian marched west to take back Prifddinas, and while he was gone his kingdom fell and Glarial was taken, so he came home to nothing and shut himself in beneath the falls. Song of the Elves has the whole of it, and the accounts of who took her don't agree.

The book deserves a note to itself. Its real title is The Missing Relics, and it says only Baxtorian and Glarial could enter the falls, and that dwarf miners may have taken his treasure early in the Fifth Age.

It also keeps Baxtorian's own Ode to Eternity and a sonnet on the two of them, on which I offer no opinion. A section on their power over nature explains why the pillars take air, water and earth runes.

{done:SONG_OF_THE_ELVES} The book can also be read in the Grand Library of Prifddinas.

{done:ROVING_ELVES} Roving Elves picks the story up. Glarial gets a new resting place in the Waterfall Dungeon, consecrated with a Moss Guardian's seed. The guardians have their own page. Islwyn, her grumpy grandson, and the kind young elf Eluned scout for the rebel elves in Isafdar.

Golrie hands out a new pebble if yours is lost, and turns up again in The Path of Glouphrie.

{done:ROVING_ELVES} Once Roving Elves starts, he and the hobgoblins swap places, and the word on him becomes "No longer locked in his own cage."

{done:BIOHAZARD,REGICIDE} The Chalice comes up again in Biohazard, where King Lathas claims his brother Tyras was corrupted when the Dark Lord forced him to drink from it. It's a lie, told to turn you against Tyras, and I've written it down as one. There is no evidence the Chalice has anything to do with the Dark Lord.

Odds and ends from the margin. Glarial's amulet looks identical to the gnome amulet, and the dungeon's fire giants are the old reliable source of rune scimitars. Once the medium Kandarin Diary is behind you as well, no rope is needed. Hudon, as far as I know, is still looking.

entries.name: Children of the Sun
entries.summary: Alina had the news first: Varlamore, shut away for hundreds of years, was sending a delegation to Varrock. Then a guard left the palace with a very large bag. You followed it, and four bandits were arrested.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
The gossip first. Alina was thrilled that Varlamore was opening to outsiders after hundreds of years. Noah asked why he should be excited about a place he'd never heard of, which I thought fair. Then the delegation arrived. I counted ten, twice.

While everyone watched the delegation, a guard left the palace with an oversized bag, told Sergeant Tobyn it was supplies, and was waved on. Noah noticed the bag. You followed it to a small building beside Aubury's and listened at the window.

Inside, four bandits planned to change into stolen guards' uniforms and strike as the delegation left the palace. The bag was the uniforms. Tobyn admitted he hadn't known the man who carried it. Varrock gets through guards so quickly, he said, that he can't keep up. I wrote that down without comment, which took some doing.

Four of the ten guards on watch were wrong in small ways. You marked them, Tobyn signalled, and they were quickly arrested. Up at the cell on the palace roof, Prince Itzla joined us from the politics downstairs and asked one bandit about local customs, then chickens, then mentioned a small fire.

The bandit told him all he knew: someone who didn't look local had paid them, and the target was the priest. Itzla said Varlamore is too civilised to burn anyone; they cut out the heart instead, while it still beats. You couldn't tell if he was joking. Nor could I, so that line is in pencil.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
Alina: the excited one. She had it all from travellers of the College of Bards, from the floating city of Tempestus, who stopped a night at the Blue Moon Inn on their way to Morytania and talked for hours.

Noah: wanted no part of any adventure, and said Varlamore sounded like a prison. He said the bag was too big before anyone else did, and nobody thanked him. I'm doing it here.

Sergeant Tobyn: keeps order round the square. He wouldn't warn the delegation, for fear of a panic, but he listened to you, which is more than most sergeants manage.

Prince Itzla Arkan: "Crown Prince Itzla Arkan, heir to the Sun Throne, at your service." He drops Varlamorian words into his talk as he goes, and doesn't stop to translate.

Servius, Teokan of Ralos: Alina said Teokan means High Priest. He never spoke in our hearing, and he was the one the bandits were paid to strike at.

{done:TWILIGHTS_PROMISE} He is also Itzla's father, which nobody mentioned on the day. Itzla calls the arrangement a convoluted mess, and I can't improve on that.

The six knights and the two others in fine dress went unnamed in Varrock. They stood very straight and said nothing at all.

{done:TWILIGHTS_PROMISE} The two were Furia and Ennius Tullus, twins. Itzla says they did the delegation's admin work, and Ennius says they organised the whole thing.

{done:THE_HEART_OF_DARKNESS} I'd have watched the twins more closely, had I known. I watched the knights instead, which was no use to anyone.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Varrock Square: Alina and Noah on the east side, behind Eliza's stall. The fountain where the King waited. Sergeant Tobyn on the north side, by the way up to the palace.

South-east Varrock: the tail runs past Lowe's Archery Emporium and Old Man Yarlo's house. It ends at a small building just east of Aubury's Rune Shop.

The east road: from the square to the east bank. The guards on watch stood along it and about the square.

Varrock Palace roof: the cell, on the west side. One bandit is in it yet, and Tobyn is still up there minding him.

The east gate: Regulus Cento waits just outside it, to the south, once it's over. The bird beside him is hard to miss.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The title seems to be Alina's. She called the delegation the children of the sun as it walked into the square, and nobody has thought of a better name.

Once the papers are signed, anyone may travel to Varlamore, and Itzla wants you there to find who paid. Regulus Cento and his bird are the only way in at first. Varlamore has its own page, written when we get there.

{done:TWILIGHTS_PROMISE} Twilight's Promise takes up who paid. You reasoned it had to be a Varlamorian who'd reached the mainland before the treaty, and Itzla said that left only the delegation: the ten I counted at the fountain. I'd counted them for no reason at the time.

Tobyn said this would be an interesting report to write. I'd read it, if only for the chickens.

entries.name: Rune Mysteries
entries.summary: Duke Horacio found an old talisman in his cellar and sent you to the Wizards' Tower with it. It had once been to an essence mine the wizards had lost, and it helped them find the way back.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
Duke Horacio had nothing he'd call a quest, but his people had turned up an old talisman while sorting the cellar. The Order of Wizards had been after magical oddments lately, so he sent it to them, by you, and told you to ask for Sedridor.

In the tower basement a wizard welcomed you to the Order's home and asked what you wanted with Sedridor, as if Sedridor were someone else. It was him. Soon he'd said your name too, which you hadn't given. I left a space in the notes for how.

He called it a plain air talisman, then murmured over it and it glowed. It had been to the lost essence mine so often that the mine had marked it. The words that take you there burned with the first tower, and the Order had been short of essence from that day on.

He kept the talisman to study and sent you to Varrock with a package for Aubury, who could hardly believe Sedridor had trusted a stranger with it. Aubury read the notes, very nearly said they'd done it, then stopped himself and sent his own notes back instead.

Then he offered you tea. Most people leave his shop rather quickly after that, I noticed. Nobody offered me any.

Back in the basement, Sedridor found the incantation in Aubury's notes. The Order has its mine again, and he'll send you there whenever you ask. He gave the talisman back, too, and said it would lead you to the Air Altar if you got lost.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
Duke Horacio: the Duke of Lumbridge. He found a thing he didn't understand and handed it to people who might, which is rarer than it should be. Lumbridge has its own page.

Archmage Sedridor: head of the Order of Wizards, who had spent a long time looking for one spell and was very pleased to find it. The name trick he put down to being the Archmage, and said no more about it.

Aubury: keeps the rune shop in south-east Varrock. "Runes are his passion," people say, and the shelves bear it out. Sedridor calls him not much of a wizard, but an expert on runecrafting. I haven't passed that on.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Lumbridge Castle: the Duke's room on the first floor. The talisman came up from the cellar, two floors below him.

The Wizards' Tower: south of Draynor Village, over the bridge, then down the ladder from the ground floor to Sedridor's rooms. The tower has its own page.

Aubury's Rune Shop: south-east Varrock, just south of the east bank. A mugger works the street outside, and doesn't follow anyone in.

The rune essence mine: on no road at all. Sedridor or Aubury says the words and you are there, among the rocks, and a portal beside them takes you back to whoever sent you. Where the mine actually is, I couldn't tell you.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Sedridor dates the Order to the rediscovery of runecrafting, just under two hundred years ago, which he says began the Fifth Age. How the first tower burned is on the Wizards' Tower page.

Before the talisman turned up, the Order bought its essence from people who would sell it but wouldn't say where they found it. Sedridor didn't name them, and I'd like to know who they are.

{done:ENTER_THE_ABYSS} The Zamorakians wanted the mine as well. In Enter the Abyss you carried their scrying orb there from three different teleporters so they could work the spell out, and they let you into the Abyss in exchange.

{done:THE_LOST_TRIBE} The Duke's cellar had more to give. In The Lost Tribe a wall down there gave way, the Duke put it down to an earthquake, and it was nothing of the kind.

Every one of the teleporters shouts the same three words as you go: "Senventior disthine molenko!" I've spelled them as best I could, and I won't be trying them.

entries.name: Sheep Shearer
entries.summary: Fred the Farmer wanted to know what you were doing on his land, and then he wanted twenty balls of wool. His sheep had the wool, Lumbridge Castle had the spinning wheel, and you did the walking.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
Fred's second question came before you'd answered his first: whether you were the one who keeps leaving his gates open. You said you were looking for a quest, which answers neither, and he let it pass. His sheep were "getting mighty woolly", he said, and he wanted twenty balls of wool off them, spun.

Then he brought up The Thing. Nobody has ever seen it, which is why it's called that. Some say it's a shapeshifter after the souls of decent folk like Fred, and some say it's a sheep. He told it with relish, then said he hadn't all day to stand about gossiping. I put a mark in the margin by that.

Anyone who turns up without shears gets a pair from Fred, and a warning: some of the sheep don't like it, and "persistence is the key". In practice the plain sheep all stand still for it, and persistence does nothing for the one that doesn't. The rams look "a little too violent to shear". I kept to the fence.

The wool went up to the spinning wheel in Lumbridge Castle and came back as balls. Fred took them in whatever handfuls you brought and told you each time how many more he needed. On the last one he said he supposed he'd better pay you. He did, and I counted the coins out of habit.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
Fred the Farmer: keeps sheep, chickens and a suspicion of anyone who sets foot on his land. Every conversation with him opens the same way, and no answer has settled it yet.

The Thing: one sheep in the pen, and the word on it is "A Sheep?", question mark and all. It won't be sheared; it just gets away. It's also the one sheep you can try to talk to, and anyone who tries concludes, sensibly, that they can't talk to sheep.

Tell Fred you've seen it and he's telling you to run for the hills and grab the chickens before you can explain. Tell him it's two penguins dressed as a sheep, and he asks, "Have you been out in the sun too long?"

{done:COLD_WAR} The penguins were operatives, as it turns out, posted in the field to watch humans and report on them. All the shearing made them suspect Fred of working for the other side. Fred, if you warn him, says he's heard that one before.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Fred's farmhouse: north-west of Lumbridge Castle. Fred is inside, and there's a pair of shears on his table. For Lumbridge, he says, follow the road east and south.

The sheep pen: built against the east side of the house. It holds the sheep, a few rams and The Thing, behind gates Fred would like kept shut.

Lumbridge Castle: the spinning wheel is on the first floor, in the room beside Duke Horacio's. Lumbridge has its own page, with the rest of the castle.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Bring twenty balls of wool to the very first conversation and the errand is over at once. Fred asks whether you've been shearing his sheep without permission, warns you not to come at him with the shears, and takes the wool.

{done:ONE_SMALL_FAVOUR} Fred turns up again in One Small Favour. The leader of H.A.M. was holding Jimmy the Chisel, said Jimmy was related to Fred, and wanted a month's supply of chickens to let him go. Fred was dismayed, hadn't enough, and sent you to Seth Groats, who had loads.

Who keeps leaving Fred's gates open, nobody has told me. He asks every stranger who turns up, so I'd guess he doesn't know either. I've been shutting them behind us.

Ram - level 2; refuses the shears, and the easiest thing in the pen to start a fight with

entries.name: Witch's House
entries.summary: A boy in Taverley kicked his ball over the wrong hedge, and the witch behind it locked it in her shed. Getting it back took two keys, a magnet, a mouse and a fight that wouldn't stay finished.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
The boy was in tears by the hedge. His ball had gone over it into the garden of an old lady he found scary, and she'd locked it in her wooden shed. You said you'd see what you could do, and he stopped crying on the spot. I've known grown men take longer.

The front door was locked, and the key was under the flower pot beside it, which is where everyone keeps theirs. The witch's diary lay on her table. I read it. Nobody stopped me. Much of it is about an experiment, some of it about locks, and one whole day is about sausages.

Her back door shows no lock and no handle, and answers to a mouse instead. Cheese fetched one out of the wall, you stuck the basement magnet to its harness, and when it went home something whirred over the door and the door gave. I wrote it all down and still don't follow it.

The garden was the slow part. The witch walks up and down the middle, so you kept behind the hedges all the way to the fountain, where the shed key was hidden. "No one will ever look there!" she'd written in her diary.

In the shed the ball sat on a crate, and the experiment sat with it. You had to beat it four times over, in a new shape each time. I kept my eyes on the door frame. I've given the experiment a page to itself.

Then out again without being caught, which would have cost you the ball, and back to the boy, who was very pleased. You told him it had been much harder than you'd thought. He didn't ask how.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
The boy: the diary calls him "That pesky kid" and says this wasn't the first time the ball came over. He called you mister, and I've let it stand.

Nora T. Hagg: the witch. We never spoke. She has a spell for anyone she finds in her garden, and shouts "Stop! Thief!" before she casts it, which I couldn't argue with. Her diary swears by Zamorak.

The mouse: "Deceptively mouse-shaped," people say. It wears a harness, works the back door for the witch, and asks nothing for it but cheese. I'd have paid it more.

{done:GRIM_TALES} Princess Miazrqa calls the witch her second cousin, twice removed. She says the ball made the witch furious, that she wouldn't let it drop, and that she even turned her own hair green.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Taverley: the boy stands by the gate in the north-east of the village, just outside the witch's hedge. The house portal is a short walk away.

The witch's house: the front door is on the west side, with the key under the pot. The diary is on the ground floor, the mouse hole in the small southern room, and the ladder down in the north room.

The basement: a gate that shocks bare hands, so gloves on first, and behind it the cupboard with the magnet. There's a piano down there too. Anyone who tries it thinks better of it, with the witch within earshot.

The garden: a long lawn between hedges, with the witch walking it. The fountain stands in a courtyard at the house end, and the shed is at the far east end.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Both locks are Professor Oddenstein's work, by the diary's account: the basement first, then the back door. He told her it was cutting edge. She called it contrived, and used it anyway.

Once it's over, the house is shut to you. Try the door and you'll decide it would be rude to break in, which it always was.

{done:GRIM_TALES} The door opened again for Grim Tales, on a house that had kept busy without us. The piano opened to the right tune, the mouse hole took anyone small enough to fit, and a gnome sat caged under the house. The diary had gone on past the 9th of Pentember, too.

The boy has his ball back. The hedge is exactly where it was.

entries.name: X Marks the Spot
entries.summary: Veos, a treasure hunter from Great Kourend, had a scroll that brought him as far as Lumbridge and no further. You dug where it pointed, four times, and he took the casket without saying what was in it.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
Veos was in the Sheared Ram with a scroll he'd found back home in Great Kourend, across the sea to the far west. It had led him to Lumbridge and stopped making sense there, because he didn't know the area. He reckoned you would, and handed it over on that guess.

The first clue was about a man named Bob, who walks out of his door, takes fourteen steps in four directions, and buries his treasure. I paced it after you and counted. It comes to four west and six north of his door, which the scroll could have said in fewer words.

The second was a map with an X behind the castle, by the kitchen's back door. Veos' advice on it, to anyone who asked, was that the X probably marked where to go. He was right, and that was all the help he gave. What came up there was an orb that runs warmer the nearer you get to the next spot, and it walked us to Draynor.

The orb's spot was just east of the village, a short way from the jail, whose guards wander. I stayed on your far side while you dug. That hole held another scroll, in cipher: ESBZOPS QJH QFO. I worked it out in the margin, every letter moved one along, and kept quiet, which was harder than the cipher.

It said Draynor pig pen. In the middle of the pen you dug up an ancient casket, and as you did there was a faint whispering. You decided it must have been the wind. I can't do better than the wind, and I've tried.

The casket went to Veos at his ship, on the northernmost pier in Port Sarim. Asked what was in it, he said "Oh err... nothing important," just something that might be useful back in Great Kourend. I doubt the first part. He did pay you, as promised.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
Veos: "An experienced treasure hunter," and experienced enough to let you do the digging. He'd come a long way on someone else's scroll, in a ship he sails between Port Sarim and Kourend.

Bob: the axe seller. The scroll used his door as a starting line, and he stayed behind his counter throughout, none the wiser.

{done:CLIENT_OF_KOUREND} Veos took on a client after this, from the mainland, he said, who wanted to know about Kourend. By the end of Client of Kourend the client was speaking through him, and once it let him go he remembered none of what he'd asked of you.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
The Sheared Ram: a pub next to the general store, where Veos waited with his scroll. A beer is two coins.

Bob's Brilliant Axes: the south end of Lumbridge. The first hole is just outside the north-west window of the house joined onto the shop.

Behind Lumbridge Castle: the kitchen's back door, with a large crate beside it. The second hole is just south-west of the crate.

East of Draynor Village: north-west of the jail and south of the wheat field, near Leela. The third hole is four steps north of a bush, where the orb runs hottest.

The Draynor pig pen: just north of the market, with Martin the Master Gardener beside it. The casket was in the middle.

Port Sarim: Veos' ship, on the northernmost pier, just south of the Rusty Anchor Inn.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Veos offered to sail you to Great Kourend whenever you like, as an extra thank you. He was going home himself, and expected to be back before long, treasure being what it is.

By the time we left his pier, Veos had an amulet on. He wasn't wearing one in the Sheared Ram, and I'd have noticed. He hasn't mentioned it, and I haven't asked.

Who wrote the scroll is still a blank in my notes. Veos found it in Kourend, and it sent him across the sea to a pig pen in Draynor. It's a long way to go to hide something.

{done:A_KINGDOM_DIVIDED} In A Kingdom Divided, Xamphur told his lord that he had planted the seeds that led a treasure hunter to him. I know one treasure hunter, and I watched you dig for him.

entries.name: Client of Kourend
entries.summary: Veos' client wanted to know how Great Kourend is run, so you toured its five cities with a scroll that stayed blank. Then came an orb for the Dark Altar, and the client said thank you in Veos' voice.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
The client wanted to know, on the quiet, how Kourend's hierarchy works and how it differs from the mainland's. The scroll saw to the quiet. Touch a feather to it and you have a quill; write with that, and the client reads every word elsewhere while the scroll stays blank. No ink needed, Veos said. I took that personally.

Veos said general store owners know their cities and like a chat, and both held. Leenz gave you Piscarilius in rhyme until you caught a verse that didn't, then asked if you'd prefer the gruff version of her. Horace was proud of the vinery, Jennifer of the soldiers, and Munty of his smiths, though he admits the sulphur mine isn't pretty work.

Regath, in Arceuus, asked why he should trust you, and you told him you were a journalist from the mainland. I let that stand. When he got to the Dark Altar, the quill and scroll glowed and burned your hand. You said you'd caught your finger, and he advised you to hold your scroll more carefully.

After the last shop a whisper sent you back to Veos, who had heard it too. The burn wasn't intentional, he passed on. Talk of the altar had "provoked emotion". Then there was an orb to activate beside it. You asked why. It was best you didn't, said Veos.

By the altar you held the orb up and it shattered, and a whisper thanked you. Back at the port, Veos said the last he'd spoken to you was on the crossing. Then he cried out, and someone else carried on in his voice. I stepped well back.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
Veos: a treasure hunter from Kourend, whose ship crosses from Port Sarim. You'd already dug up a casket for him in a Draynor pig pen, and he called what was in it nothing important. Asked whether you were spying, he said not exactly. At the end he remembered none of it.

Veos' Client: Veos only ever called it his client, so that's where I've filed it. It thanked you, promised no harm would come to Veos, and would not say who it was. "Knowledge can be a curse," it said, to a scribe.

The shopkeepers: each named their city's leader for the scroll, and Leenz called hers ruthless with some pride. All five names are on the Great Kourend page, which also covers what the cities are for.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Port Sarim: Veos' ship, at the northernmost pier. He hopes you don't get seasick, and says it's a long voyage.

Port Piscarilius: where the ship comes in and Veos waits on the dock. Leenz's store is further up the town.

Hosidius, Shayzien and Lovakengj: a general store in each, and a minecart between them for anyone who would rather not walk it.

Arceuus: Regath's Wares, on the south-east side of the city. It's the shop I remember best.

The Dark Altar: north of Arceuus, in a field of dark crystals, with Tyss beside it. I stayed at the edge of the crystals, and I'd do the same again.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Veos paid you in lamps and an old book he'd bought at auction. It belonged, he says, to the daughter of King Kharedst IV, the last king before the Council, and most of its pages are missing. I'd have taken it for the missing pages alone.

{done:A_KINGDOM_DIVIDED} The client wasn't done with Veos. After the earthquake Veos wandered off in a trance, Cabin Boy Herbert says, and you found him with Xamphur, who addressed him as his lord. Xamphur once served Xeric, by Lord Arceuus' account, and the Tasakaal confirmed it. Nobody said the client's name aloud, so I haven't written it either.

entries.name: Giant Mole
entries.summary: A mole the size of a hay cart, living in the tunnels under Falador Park. Wyson the gardener grew it by accident with a bottle of growth potion, which is the kind of accident I keep notes on.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
The Giant Mole, or Talpidae wysonian if you want the scientific name, after Wyson. The note on it just reads "Holy Mole-y!" I didn't write that.

Its main trick is to burrow off through the tunnels when it is hurt. It puts out any candle, torch or oil lamp within reach when it comes up, so I stood back with ours.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
The Mole Hole, under Falador Park. Dig with a spade on one of the mole hills in the park and you drop straight in.

The tunnels are dark. Without a light you will be hurt as you walk them, so bring one.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The histories call it a slight accident. Wyson poured a bottle of Malignius-Mortifer's-Super-Ultra-Flora-Growth-Potion on his plants. The name of the potion should have been a warning.

Wyson trades the mole's skins and claws for bird nests, which is a tidy arrangement for the man who caused the problem.

Three tiles across
Always drops a mole skin and a mole claw
One kill completes a hard Falador Diary task

entries.name: King Black Dragon

tally.label: Dragon kings put down, all told

entries.summary: It's the size of a house, and in the old days nothing anyone knew of was stronger. Its lair sits behind a lever in the deep Wilderness, and the walk there is the first test.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
People describe it as "One of the biggest, meanest dragons around." I stood well back and found nothing to correct. It will set on you unprovoked and its bite poisons.

It has four breaths: ordinary dragonfire, then shock, ice and poison. Its weakness is water spells, which seems fair for something that breathes fire.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
The King Black Dragon Lair, reached through the deep Wilderness near the Lava Maze. Climb down the ladder near the lesser demons, then pull the lever surrounded by poisonous spiders. The lair itself is not Wilderness. The approach very much is.

Common routes in: a burning amulet to the Lava Maze, the lever north-west of Ardougne Castle to the Deserted Keep, the Edgeville canoe, or the Wilderness obelisks. 50,000 coins buys you the lair to yourself. Steep, but nobody else gets a swing at your dragon.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
It lost the title of strongest when the Kalphite Queen turned up. I have that in the margin, underlined.

{done:A_TAIL_OF_TWO_CATS} It can talk. In A Tail of Two Cats it holds a conversation with Bob the cat, and gets interrupted before it finishes. I'd have liked the minutes of that one.

Going in was your idea. What I thought on the way, I've kept to myself.

entries.name: Goblin

tally.label: Goblins you've killed while I watched

entries.summary: The war god Bandos brought goblins to the world, and now there's hardly a road without one. Their main village in Asgarnia is run by two generals who cannot agree on anything, and somehow it still stands.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: The word on them is "An ugly green creature." Blunt, but not wrong. New adventurers learning to fight go looking for them, which is a polite way of putting it.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
Everywhere a new adventurer is likely to tread. Lumbridge alone has over a hundred of them, and there are more between Lumbridge and Varrock, west of Varrock, at the Digsite, Port Sarim, Draynor Village and Lumbridge Swamp.

Further afield too: the Goblin Cave, near the Fishing Guild, the Tree Gnome Village maze, the Clock Tower Dungeon, Hosidius, the Kebos Lowlands, the Hollows, the Observatory Dungeon and the Underground Pass. You are never far from one.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Goblins follow Bandos, the Big High War God. He arrived on Gielinor in the Second Age to wage war, and brought armies of goblins, ogres, orks and ourgs with him. Goblins aren't strong, so they make up for it with numbers, which is the oldest trick there is.

Goblin Village has two generals, Bentnoze and Wartface, and they butt heads over anything trivial, armour colours included.

{done:GOBLIN_DIPLOMACY} Settling that argument is the whole of the quest Goblin Diplomacy. Diplomacy is a generous word for it.

{done:THE_LOST_TRIBE,LAND_OF_THE_GOBLINS} Not all goblins stayed loyal to Bandos. The Dorgeshuun cave goblins turned their backs on his teachings and went back to the cooperative ways of their Yu'biusk past. Sensible, and rare.

I've watched a fair few goblins lose a fight. Not one has looked surprised about it.

General Wartface - of the Garagorshuun tribe. The other half.
places: {done:THE_LOST_TRIBE,DEATH_TO_THE_DORGESHUUN} Dorgesh-Kaan - home of the Dorgeshuun cave goblins

entries.name: Hill Giant

tally.label: Hill giants felled while I watched

entries.summary: Dungeons and hills are full of them, each "A very large foe". Of the three giant kinds most adventurers meet first it's the weakest, which isn't the same as weak. Their giant keys open the door to Obor, the Hill Titan.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: The Kourend sort are said to be "A very large foe that has been corrupted by the Dark Altar", which is the same giant in a worse neighbourhood. Now and then one leaves more than bones behind. Worth checking the pile.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
The Edgeville Dungeon has the most of them close to home. The Shayzien Giant Pit has more still.

Also in the Giants' Den, the Catacombs of Kourend, the Giants' Plateau, Taverley Dungeon, the Deep Wilderness Dungeon, the Lava Maze, the Gnome Maze, north of the Observatory, south-west of the Tree Gnome Stronghold, the Bone Yard and the Avium Savannah.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The old histories just call them Giants. "Hill" went on the front of the name to tell them from the other kinds, and some say it's for their arm muscles, which look like hills. I've looked. I suppose they do.

Despite the name, most of them live in dungeons, and some carry cleavers. The other two kinds are moss giants and ice giants. I'd have called these ones dungeon giants, but nobody asked me.

{done:RECIPE_FOR_DISASTER} The cleavers come from Recipe for Disaster.

entries.name: Fire Giant

tally.label: Fire giants put out while I watched

entries.summary: The strongest of the ordinary giants, an elemental brute in the Brimhaven Dungeon and a good many other caves. Slayers and archers favour it, and it's the classic source of a rune scimitar. Everyone goes back eventually.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: "A very large elemental adversary" is the usual description, and it's the heat you notice first. There are three sorts, all of them aggressive and none of them quick to swing. Nothing burns it, and water magic bites. No surprises on either count.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
{done:WATERFALL_QUEST} The Waterfall Dungeon has eleven. They guard Baxtorian's western passage and the chalice room.

The Brimhaven Dungeon, the Catacombs of Kourend, the Charred Dungeon, the Deep Wilderness Dungeon, the Giants' Den, the Isle of Souls Dungeon, the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon, the Smoke Dungeon and the Stronghold Slayer Dungeon all keep them. Only in the Charred Dungeon can more than one set on you at once.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The drop that matters is the rune scimitar. Beyond that: the fire battlestaff, the steel axe, the mithril square shield, fire and chaos runes and the odd gem.

I tried to draw one from close up, and the ink dried on the nib. The plate was done from further off.

Levels 104 and 109 - the other two sorts
Rune scimitar - rare, about one in 128
Slayer - no level needed, and Slayer masters assign them

entries.name: Monk of Zamorak

tally.label: Monks seen off while I watched

entries.summary:
They're evil human clerics of Zamorak, and weak on paper. The paper is wrong.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} A band of them seized Paterdomus in Priest in Peril and poisoned the River Salve. That's the sort they are.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Everyone has them down as "An evil human cleric." They switch between melee and magic and hit harder than their level suggests.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
The Chaos Temple in Asgarnia, the cage under the stairs in Varrock Palace, Taverley Dungeon and the Deep Wilderness Dungeon.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} Paterdomus too, the temple on the River Salve, all through Priest in Peril; they had the run of the place.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} At Paterdomus the hooded one at the door passed himself off as Drezel, the priest they had imprisoned. The rest is on the Priest in Peril page.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL,THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES} The ones at Paterdomus heal quickly and are poor value. The Blood Moon Rises cleared them out for good, and not before time.

Many an adventurer trains magic by casting Curse on the caged one in Varrock Palace. He's in no position to object.

people: Zamorak - the god they serve. Chaos, by trade.
details: Levels 17, 22, 23, 30 and 45
{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} The hooded one at Paterdomus - level 30
Bones - always
Zamorak monk top and bottom - about one in twenty each
{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} Paterdomus monks - 25 percent of normal combat experience

entries.name: Temple Guardian
entries.summary: A big dog in the mausoleum under Paterdomus, on the River Salve. Worth a page, I thought.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Everyone puts it the same way: "Looks like a big ugly dog." It stabs, and quickly.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: Below Paterdomus, the temple on Misthalin's eastern border, down the trapdoor north of it. It turns up only during Priest in Peril. Found once, then.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} By King Roald's account it guarded the way into the mausoleum and the river's source. The rest belongs to Priest in Peril, which has its own page.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} Roald called it Spots. He also called it a pedigree light beast, or was it dark beast. His words, not mine.

Dark beasts, I am told, once looked much like it, only brown. I have not seen a dark beast, and I am in no hurry to.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} While you fought it, I studied the ceiling of the mausoleum. It is well made.

details: Level 30 - 45 hitpoints, hits up to 3
Immune - magic and dwarf cannons
Ring of recoil - does the job, once you land a hit yourself
Slayer - counts among the dogs, for what that is worth
{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} Owner - King Roald

entries.name: Moss Guardian
entries.summary:
The guardian spirits of Glarial's Tomb, and a good deal stronger than the ordinary moss giant.

{done:ROVING_ELVES} In Roving Elves, Islwyn and Eluned send you to kill one for a consecration seed, and they mean bare-handed.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Described as "Bigger than your average moss giant." Slow to swing, and always aggressive. Each blow comes at you as melee, and if it misses, it tries again against your magic defence. Protect from Melee stops only the first part. Underlined.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
Glarial's Tomb, south-east of Baxtorian Falls and north-west of the Fishing Guild, under a tombstone. Three of them, and nowhere else.

{done:WATERFALL_QUEST} The tomb lets in no weapons, armour, runes or ammunition, so you meet them bare-handed. Bring food, and potions.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
They guard Glarial, the queen whose tomb it is. The Waterfall Quest has its own page.

The tomb let me in with the notebook and nothing else. I've decided to take that as approval.

details: Level 84 - 120 hitpoints, hits up to 14
Attack, Strength and Defence - 60 each
Drops - big bones
{done:ROVING_ELVES} Consecration seed - dropped only during Roving Elves

entries.name: Witch's Experiment
entries.summary: The name says whose it is. Nora T. Hagg keeps it in her locked garden shed in Taverley, and it doesn't care for visitors.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
I met it from the shed doorway, which is as far in as I go. The witch's diary had warned me: she raised it on fungus, tar and clay, and moved it out of the house when it began breaking things. Not clever yet, she wrote, but with "a really mean stare".

{done:WITCHS_HOUSE} It won't keep a shape. Beat it and it gets up as a spider, then a bear, then a wolf, and only the wolf stays down. I counted the floorboards it covered each time: by the end, four times what it started on.

{done:WITCHS_HOUSE} The stare is real. Reach for the ball while it's about and it only looks at you, and you come away weaker. I still don't know how a look does that.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: The wooden shed at the east end of Nora T. Hagg's garden, in north Taverley, behind a locked door. Once Witch's House is done it can be met again in the Nightmare Zone at Yanille, as one of Dominic Onion's dreams.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The quest is written up under Witch's House. On the 9th of Pentember the witch still hadn't settled on a name for it: Fritz, probably, though Lucy, she wrote, reminded her of her mother.

{done:GRIM_TALES} Fritz it was. Later pages of the diary mourn him by name, blame "a wretched adventurer" and promise revenge. She also admits that something odd about him worried her, and leaves it there.

{done:GRIM_TALES} She didn't stop at one. The next lot live in the sewers under her house and came out, she wrote, as more than one creature apiece. I haven't been down to look.

people: Nora T. Hagg - made it, fed it and keeps it in the shed
details: Level 19 - 21 hitpoints, hits up to 2, and always aggressive
{done:WITCHS_HOUSE} After that - levels 30, 42 and 53, hitting up to 3, 4 and 5
{done:WITCHS_HOUSE} All four shapes - 144 hitpoints between them; melee attacks only
{done:WITCHS_HOUSE} Leave mid-fight - it starts again from the first shape
Dwarf cannons - can't be set up in the shed
Nightmare Zone - a normal version and a hard one, after the quest

entries.name: Lumbridge
entries.summary: Everyone starts out in Lumbridge, in Misthalin, and the dead come back here too, so it gets a lot of traffic. It's named for the bridge over the River Lum, and Duke Horacio rules from the castle.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Tutorial Island sends its new arrivals here, and the dead come back here too, unless they have arranged otherwise. So most people see it at least twice, once on the way in and once after the first mistake.

Duke Horacio descends directly from Polonius, the first Duke. King Claudius of Varrock gave Polonius the land, and he swapped the old wooden fort for Lumbridge Castle. It's the kind of thing a duke likes written down, so I have.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: South of Varrock, east of Draynor Village and west of Al Kharid, with Lumbridge Swamp and its caves to the south. You'll know it by the castle, the church of Saradomin, the cow field and the general store.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:THE_LOST_TRIBE} During the God Wars, the caves beneath what is now the town sheltered a lost goblin tribe.

Long after the God Wars, migrating human nomads settled on the River Lum. They built a bridge across it, then named the town after the bridge. Practical people. Good bridge.

Father Aereck keeps the church of Saradomin, which is over 230 years old and still standing. Several quests start here too, which is a lot for one town with one bridge.

{done:LOST_CITY} An unassuming shed in the swamp leads to the fairy city of Zanaris. I wouldn't have guessed it from the shed.

people: The Lumbridge Guide - helps new adventurers and turns up in several quests
details: Founded - the year 1937 of the Fourth Age
{done:LOST_CITY} The shed to Zanaris - opens once Lost City is done
Quests - Cook's Assistant, The Restless Ghost, Sheep Shearer, Rune Mysteries
Also from here - X Marks the Spot, in the Sheared Ram

plates.caption: Lumbridge, done in a hurry.
plates.hint: Pose for me in Lumbridge.

entries.name: Varrock
entries.summary: Varrock is the capital of Misthalin and one of the biggest cities in Gielinor. It began as Avarrocka, a forest camp. It's loud and busy now, and I'm fond of it.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Varrock is said vah-ROCK. King Roald lives in Varrock Palace, at the heart of the city. You can't miss it, though people try.

The Grand Exchange stands inside the walls, and so do a Saradomin church and a Zamorakian chapel. Both faiths, one set of walls. I haven't asked how that works.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: Central Misthalin. The Wilderness lies to the north, Barbarian Village to the north-west, the Digsite to the east and Lumbridge to the south.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Avarrocka began when a nomadic tribe found a boy of exceptional strength, took him for a good omen and settled in the forest there. The boy was Arrav, and as he grew, so did Avarrocka.

{done:DEFENDER_OF_VARROCK} Ten years after the founding, goblins attacked. The boy beat them off, and that's how he came by the name Arrav.

{done:SHIELD_OF_ARRAV,DEFENDER_OF_VARROCK} Then Zemouregal came, a Mahjarrat necromancer of Zamorak's, with an army of zombies. His forces were beaten, but Arrav fell and was taken as an undead servant. A poor ending for the boy. The city rebuilt and kept growing, and in time it had a king and a kingdom, Misthalin.

Avarrocka has shortened to Varrock, but the boy hasn't been forgotten, and people still talk about the Shield of Arrav. One day I'd like an afternoon on the fountain's edge with nobody in a hurry. I'd still take notes.

places: Grand Exchange - the great trading floor
Varrock Museum - natural history displays and a quiz
Champions' Guild - sells rune weapons and green dragonhide
Blue Moon Inn - the most popular pub in Varrock
Varrock Sewers - home of Scurrius and Bryophyta
details: Ruler - King Roald
Founded - the year 700 of the Fourth Age, as Avarrocka
Quests - Demon Slayer, Dragon Slayer I, Romeo & Juliet, Shield of Arrav
More quests - Defender of Varrock, Family Crest, Priest in Peril

plates.caption: The square. Only we stood still.
plates.hint: Pose for me in the square.

plates.caption: The palace end. Best behaviour.
plates.hint: Pose for me by the palace.

plates.caption: King Roald. I bowed, to be safe.
The Exchange. I bought nothing.
plates.hint: Pose for me at the Exchange.

entries.name: Paterdomus
entries.summary:
The temple of Saradomin on the River Salve, at Misthalin's eastern edge. It is the only gate into Morytania.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} It stands over the graves of the Seven Priestly Warriors. I lower my voice in there.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
The name comes from an old tongue, pater plus domus. House of the Father, meaning Saradomin.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} You need Drezel's blessing to cross its bridge, and he is the temple's only priest, so there is no one else to ask.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} Four floors: an altar on the ground floor, a cell and a vampyre coffin at the top, and monks of Zamorak on every floor from the ground up. Not what you expect in a house of Saradomin, but there it is.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} Outside are more coffins. They hold vampyres stranded west of the river, too weak to move and impossible to kill, which is a combination I don't like.

There is a statue of Saradomin by the water, and a railing shortcut. A trapdoor to the north leads down to the basement mausoleum.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} Down there are the guardian's chamber, a well ringed by seven monuments, and a passage to the north-east.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL,IN_AID_OF_THE_MYREQUE} There is a hidden library down there as well.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: It stands on the River Salve at the eastern end of Silvarea, the pass that leads to it. Canifis is just across the river.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} The Seven Priestly Warriors blessed the Salve here, and the temple was built in their honour. The monuments round the well in the mausoleum are theirs. They have their own page.

Priest in Peril, Nature Spirit, In Aid of the Myreque, Darkness of Hallowvale, Sins of the Father, Devious Minds and The Blood Moon Rises all come through here. So do my notes.

details: Railing shortcut - 65 Agility
Temple Trekking - the finish line

plates.caption: The temple. No monks sat for it.
plates.hint: Pose for me by the temple.

plates.caption: Drezel. The King asked after him.

entries.name: Baxtorian Falls
entries.summary: The rapids run south from the Lunar Sea to the River Dougne, north-west of Ardougne in Kandarin. They're named for the elven king who sealed himself beneath them, which tells you something about the place.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
A lot is packed round these rapids. Almera lives at the top, and her son Hudon is out on the island after treasure. Hadley's Tourist Information Centre and Gerald the fisherman are just south. Rasolo the merchant is by the centre, and overpriced. I checked.

There is a second waterfall that flows east from the lake. The west bank is for Barbarian fishing, the leaping kind, and the whirlpool takes you down into the Ancient Cavern. On purpose, I'm told.

{done:WATERFALL_QUEST} Glarial's Tomb is a short way south-east, under a tombstone.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: East of the Tree Gnome Stronghold and south of the Barbarian Outpost. Get there by games necklace, or on foot from Seers' Village if you want the walk.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Almera says Hudon can't swim. I doubt the falls have taken that into account.

{done:SONG_OF_THE_ELVES} The king in question goes by Lord Baxtorian Cadarn these days, and he is no longer under the falls.

details: Barbarian fishing - fast Fishing training, with a Barbarian rod
Ancient Cavern whirlpool - after Barbarian Training
Barrel - off the ledge and down the river, if you are the sort

plates.caption: The falls. The ink ran.
plates.hint: Pose for me by the falls.

entries.name: Wizards' Tower
entries.summary: There's an eye on the front of the Wizards' Tower, facing the bridge, and it was the first thing I noticed. The tower is the home of the Order of Wizards, on its own island south of Draynor Village.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Anyone crossing the bridge gets a good look at the eye, and it at them. I stood under it a while and couldn't decide whether it was meant as a welcome or a warning. What it's an eye of is anyone's guess, mine included.

Inside, the ground floor is a library and a good many wizards in blue. Wizard Traiborn keeps the first floor. The second keeps a lesser demon in a cage, which it bears better than I would.

Archmage Sedridor, who leads the Order, works down a ladder in the basement. He tells visitors to take care, because they're standing on the ruins of an older tower. He says it kindly, which doesn't help.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: South of Draynor Village, across a bridge from the mainland, with Port Sarim to the west and Lumbridge Swamp to the east. The fairy ring DIS sets down just south of the tower, and a necklace of passage at the bridge.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The library on the ground floor is what I'd come back for. I've read the spines. Only the spines.

{done:RUNE_MYSTERIES} Sedridor says the first tower went up when runecrafting was found again, at the start of the Fifth Age, and that the Order's own Zamorakian wizards burnt it down. The basement is all that's left of it, and he still works there. Rune Mysteries has its own page.

{done:ENTER_THE_ABYSS} The Zamorakians tell it another way. One of theirs made a breakthrough in teleport magic, they say, the Order stole it, and a ritual built on it went wrong and burnt the place down. Sedridor calls that hearsay. I've written down both and taken no side.

{done:TEMPLE_OF_THE_EYE} A portal in the basement now leads to the Temple of the Eye, where the Order and the Guardians of the Rift hold back the Abyss. The first tower knew the Eye well enough to borrow its symbol for the Order, Sedridor says, and nobody does now. I take that to be the eye by the bridge.

people: Archmage Sedridor - head of the Order of Wizards, in the basement
Wizard Traiborn - first floor, mislaying things
Wizard Mizgog - second floor, next door to the demon
places: Library - the ground floor, bookcases and all
Basement - Sedridor's rooms, down the ladder from the ground floor
{done:TEMPLE_OF_THE_EYE} Temple of the Eye - through the portal in the basement
details: Ways in - the fairy ring DIS, or a necklace of passage to the bridge
Wizards' Guild - its east portal comes here, at 66 Magic
Lesser demon - level 82, caged; only spells and ranged attacks reach it
Quests - Rune Mysteries, Imp Catcher, The Restless Ghost, Demon Slayer
{done:RUNE_MYSTERIES} Essence mine - Sedridor sends you on request

plates.caption: The tower, and the eye on it.
plates.hint: Pose for me by the tower.

entries.name: Seven Priestly Warriors
entries.summary:
In the Fourth Age, seven priestly warriors of Saradomin held Lord Drakan's vampyres at the River Salve and blessed it so no vampyre could cross. It cost them their lives.

{done:THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES} They were Temple Knights, and only six of them died in the fight itself.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Paterdomus now stands on the ground they held. Their names: Ivandis Seergaze, Iriandul Caistlyn, Sarl Dunegun, Derygull Templeton, Erysail the Pious, Friar Twiblick and Essiandar Gar. I have written all seven names out in full. They earned that much.

They were active around 1200 of the Fourth Age, in the Misthalin-Morytania War, when Drakan had crossed the Salve and pushed west towards Varrock.

{done:THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES} The Temple Knights sent them to secure the river. Secretly, they were also to research haemalchemy, which their leaders believed held the key to beating vampyres.

{done:THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES} Their savants designed a blood ritual to bar vampyres from the river. The warriors told the soldiers it was a holy consecration by Saradomin, and kept quiet about what it really was. A blood rite with a clean name. It worked, which is the uncomfortable part.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES} At the river's source the vampyres attacked mid-ritual. Derygull fell first, then the others, one by one, until only Ivandis was left. He laid the six to rest around the ritual well.

{done:THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES,IN_AID_OF_THE_MYREQUE} Ivandis was showing signs of vampyrification. He refused to become what they had sworn to destroy, and charged into Morytania to kill Drakan. He died in the attempt, and his coffin lies in caves beneath the Hollows. I have no remark for that one.

Later histories say the blessing sealed the vengeful power of Saradomin in the river. Drezel of Paterdomus is descended from one of the seven. Their monuments stand round the well below the temple. I counted seven, and went no closer.

{done:SINS_OF_THE_FATHER} Ivan Strom is Ivandis's last living descendant. That should be better known.

people: {done:IN_AID_OF_THE_MYREQUE} Ivandis Seergaze - from what is now Lumbridge
details: Misthalin-Morytania War - about 1100 to 1200 of the Fourth Age
Last battle - Silvarea

plates.caption: The temple over their graves.
plates.hint: Pose for me by the temple.

entries.name: Morytania
entries.summary: Morytania lies in the far east of Gielinor, and Lord Drakan's vampyres rule it. Only the blessed River Salve keeps them out of Misthalin, and I'm grateful to that river.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
The name is said mor-ee-TAY-nee-ah. The land is full of things that go for you on sight. None of the towns is restful, and the walks between them are no better than the stops.

{done:DARKNESS_OF_HALLOWVALE,A_TASTE_OF_HOPE,SINS_OF_THE_FATHER} Drakan's sister Vanescula calls him Lowerniel. She and their brother Ranis once ran things for him. Ranis is dead now, and Vanescula turned against him.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: East of Misthalin, across the River Salve. The way in is the temple of Paterdomus on the river.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:IN_AID_OF_THE_MYREQUE,DARKNESS_OF_HALLOWVALE,SINS_OF_THE_FATHER} Before the God Wars this was Hallowvale, or the Hallowland, a Saradominist kingdom under the Icyene Queen Efaritay. In the Third Age Lord Drakan conquered it with vampyres and werewolves. He turned the fertile land into swamp and kept its people as a blood farm. That is the history of the place in three sentences, and none of them get better.

{done:IN_SEARCH_OF_THE_MYREQUE,DARKNESS_OF_HALLOWVALE,SINS_OF_THE_FATHER} Drakan himself is a true-born vampyre. Zaros brought him from Vampyrium in the Second Age, and he sided with Zamorak in exchange for these lands. He captured Efaritay's husband Ascertes, who became the vampyre Vanstrom Klause.

The Salve was blessed against Drakan's invasion by the Seven Priestly Warriors, who have their own page. Its water burns creatures of Zamorak on contact, and no vampyre can cross it. Whenever we cross, I will be watching the water.

Werewolves can still cross, and do, kidnapping people and smuggling for the vampyres; some have turned up as far away as under the Champions' Guild. Roavar says Drakan's brother Draynor ended up trapped on the Misthalin side of the river.

{done:SINS_OF_THE_FATHER} Vanescula says Draynor was weak even before the Salve trapped him, and a coward as well. There was a reason, she says, that Lowerniel had him banished.

The Salve flows past where Senntisten once stood, and the Digsite excavations reach its bank. The river has more history than most kingdoms.

{done:HAUNTED_MINE} Blessed water seeping through the rock of the Mort Ridge Mine forms Salve shards, crystals with power over evil. The Salve amulet is made from one, and the undead don't care for it.

The Barrows brothers tried to liberate the land, and died for it. The Myreque now fight to throw off vampyre rule. I hope they get a longer page than the brothers did.

Roavar - the barman in Canifis

{done:DARKNESS_OF_HALLOWVALE} Meiyerditch - the blood farm city, a blood-tithed ghetto
Port Phasmatys - the cursed port of ghosts
Mort Myre Swamp - the great swamp south of Canifis

{done:IN_SEARCH_OF_THE_MYREQUE,IN_AID_OF_THE_MYREQUE} Burgh de Rott - the last free human settlement, home of the Myreque

entries.name: Varlamore
entries.summary: Regulus Cento's bird lands beside the Sunrise Palace gardens, which is where I started counting statues. Varlamore is the kingdom across the western sea, south of Great Kourend, and Civitas illa Fortis is its capital.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
The palace garden has Queen Zyanyi in the middle of it, in stone, and the way in has Prince Itzla on either side. Past him are the queen again and three heroes I'd never heard of: Xerna, Marhuitz and Taur.

{done:CHILDREN_OF_THE_SUN} On a palace roof in Varrock I watched the prince question a bandit, and enjoy it. The sculptor has given him a graver face.

Alina, in Varrock Square, had it from travelling bards that the kingdom was closed for hundreds of years, that a Sun Queen rules it from the capital, and that its people worship the sun and the moon. Nothing I've seen here says she was wrong. I'd like to see it at sunrise, given what they named the palace.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: West over the sea from the mainland, south of Great Kourend and past the mountains. The way in is Regulus Cento, outside Varrock's east gate with his quetzal, Primio. Every other road in opens only after that first flight.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Primio is "A big pretty bird" to everyone who meets him. I paced round him while Regulus wasn't looking: three paces a side, and the bird let me. Regulus keeps him, and so keeps the door.

{done:TWILIGHTS_PROMISE} The queen in the garden is Itzla's mother, which explains the two of him on the way in.

The quest that opened the kingdom, Children of the Sun, has its own page. People here mostly say Fortis and keep the full name for maps and visitors. I say all of it, every time, and I still don't know what the rest of it means.

people: Regulus Cento - Primio's keeper, at both ends of the flight
Queen Zyanyi - the Sun Queen; two statues of her at the palace
places: Civitas illa Fortis - the capital; Fortis, to its own people
Sunrise Palace - the royal residence, statues and all
Bazaar - the market, south of where the bird lands
Fortis Colosseum - on the cliffs at the east end of the city
Hunter Guild - south-west of the city
details: Way in - Regulus Cento and Primio, outside Varrock's east gate, after Children of the Sun
Other routes - fairy rings, charter ships and the rest, only after that first flight

plates.caption: Fortis. More statues than I drew.
plates.hint: Pose for me in Civitas illa Fortis.

entries.name: Great Kourend
entries.summary: "Beware of the thieves," Veos says of Port Piscarilius, where his ship puts in. Great Kourend is five cities under five ruling houses, and this port is one of them.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
On his word I carried the book under my arm all the way up the quay, and I watched every hand I passed. Nobody tried for it. I've decided that was the arm. Leenz, at the general store further up, says hello in rhyme. I checked my pockets after that too.

Veos gives the cities in order from the port. West is Arceuus, where they study magic at the Grand Library, and further west Lovakengj, mining and smithing to arm the Shayzien soldiers in the south-west. South is Hosidius, which farms for the lot of them.

A king or queen once ruled all five, Veos says. The last king died twenty years ago, and the Kourend Council has run the kingdom in the meantime. Who sits on it, he didn't say.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: Across the sea to the west of the mainland, with Varlamore to the south; Varlamore has its own page. Veos' ship sails from the northernmost pier in Port Sarim to Port Piscarilius, or to Land's End in the south-west.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Next time I'd like to walk up that quay slowly, with both hands free. I don't expect to.

{done:CLIENT_OF_KOUREND} The shopkeepers named the five leaders for us: Shauna Piscarilius, Kandur Hosidius, Shiro Shayzien, Vulcana Lovakengj and Trobin Arceuus. How we came to ask is on the Client of Kourend page.

{done:THE_QUEEN_OF_THIEVES} The Queen of Thieves, who leads the biggest gang in the port, told us herself that she is Lady Shauna Piscarilius. I've stopped carrying the book under my arm in her port. It wouldn't help.
